subject: Token runway & peak TPS — budget floor/ceiling check
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Patel <morgan@clovertech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (tokens & peak TPS)

Hi Morgan — thanks again for the demo this morning. Wanted to capture the assumptions we discussed and confirm a few items so we can put together a clean hosted pricing illustration. TL;DR below, details/asks after.

TL;DR
- Your rough monthly token range (post-demo): 120M–180M tokens/month
- Peak 99th-percentile TPS (burst): ~350 TPS for short windows (60–90s)
- Target $/1M tokens target band you mentioned on the call: $9–$14
- Next steps: confirm exact expected sustained concurrency (avg QPS), whether spikes are client-driven or scheduled batch, and whether you can sign a 6–12 month commit if we propose a slab.

Assumptions I used on the call (please correct where off):
- Typical request size: 400 tokens inbound + 1,200 tokens generated = ~1.6k tokens per API call
- Daily traffic profile: 90% of traffic steady-state; 10% in short burst windows tied to hourly customer syncs
- Retention: you do not need query/response retention on-hosted beyond default 30 days

Concrete questions we need to finalize pricing:
1) On average, how many concurrent open requests do you expect during steady-state (avg QPS)?
2) For the bursts: are they predictable (e.g., cron / batch) or are they unpredictable (user-driven)? If predictable, how many windows per day and duration?
3) Is the $9–$14 /1M tokens an absolute cap you have to hit for procurement? or a flexible target depending on SLA/throughput guarantees?
4) Any compliance requirements (SOC2, data residency) that would push this to a Private deployment vs. Hosted?

Attachments: I’ve attached the consumption breakdown template so you can drop sample counts (clovertech_consumption_breakdown.csv) and I included the demo recording.

If you’re good with the numbers above, we’ll prepare two options:
A) Small commit (6 months) — slightly higher $/1M but with 60s burst allowance at no extra cost
B) Committed slab (12 months) — lower $/1M with defined burst capacity and a simple overage matrix

Would it be possible to get the consumption CSV back by EOD Monday? If that works, we’ll aim to send an initial hosted pricing illustration by Wednesday.

Thanks — enjoyed the conversation.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: Morgan Patel <morgan@clovertech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clovertech.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (tokens & peak TPS)

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear recap. Minor corrections and extra detail below.

Confirmed numbers:
- Expected monthly tokens: ~150M (range we’d expect to land in: 130M–170M)
- Typical request payload: 300 tokens in, 900 tokens out (we were conservative on the call) — ~1.2k total tokens/call
- Steady-state avg QPS: ~120 QPS (sustained over business hours), which maps to ~10k QPS-minute in our current profiling
- Spikes: yes — we have a scheduled hourly sync that fans out notifications resulting in ~300–400 TPS for ~45–90s; once every hour during business hours (~8 windows/day). It’s predictable and we can schedule it slightly to avoid simultaneous downstream events.
- Budget band: procurement is comfortable up to $12 / 1M tokens for hosted with standard SOC2 and 99th-pct latency SLO (we can stretch to $14 if there is a hard SLA and burst guarantees).

Procurement notes:
- We typically prefer a 12-month committed slab but can do a 6-month POC if Redwood can provide a clear path to the lower $/1M at renewal.
- Need to see a clear overage policy for bursts (how billing works if bursts exceed the bundled burst allowance)

I’ve attached a short sample output from our traffic simulator — should help you model the 8 daily windows.

If you can put together two price cards (6m POC and 12m committed) with the burst mechanics spelled out, that should get procurement to a decision point.

Thanks — Morgan

--
Morgan Patel
Head of Product, CloverTech
morgan@clovertech.com | +1 (617) 555-3301
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (tokens & peak TPS) — CloverTech confirmed numbers

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Morgan’s confirmation. Key pieces: 150M monthly (130–170M range), steady 120 QPS, 8 predictable hourly spikes/day at ~350 TPS for 45–90s, procurement target $12 /1M (stretch to $14 with SLA). They prefer 12-month commit but will accept 6-month POC if renewal path to lower price is clear.

Attachments (from Morgan): clovertech_consumption_breakdown.csv, clovertech_simulator_output.csv, mvp_requirements_clovertech.pdf

Proposed immediate ask for pricing ops:
- Can we model a 12-month slab at $10.50 /1M tokens with an included burst pool that covers 8x 90s windows/day at up to 400 TPS (addressing both predictability and safety margin)?
- Alternative 6-month POC at $12.50 /1M with burst covered but higher overage rate (propose $18 /1M overage).
- What does the SLA/credit profile look like if we include 99th-pct latency guarantee for their 120 QPS steady-state?

I’ll assemble the usage curves from their CSV and send to pricing/ops for a formal illustration. Putting this on your radar for recommended slab pricing and any concerns re: hosted capacity (we should verify capacity on east-us region for these burst windows).

If you want to jump on a 20-min quick to align, I’m free 11:00–11:30 PT today.

—
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
